NSE: JIOFIN | BSE: 543940 | Price as of 19 Oct 2026 close | Report date:
JFSL is building a broad financial-services platform around Jio distribution, a large capital base and joint ventures with
BlackRock and Allianz. Q2 FY27 showed strong operating expansion: Jio Credit AUM reached Rs 37,320 crore and
disbursements nearly doubled year on year. Yet the consolidated earnings base remains uneven: Q2 PAT fell 51% year on
year, and new businesses plus JVs continue to consume investment. At Rs 214, the market already prices in substantial
execution. Our illustrative FY29 earnings scenarios give a wide value range; the base case implies only modest upside,
Key debate: Can faster lending and fee growth turn into durable group earnings before funding costs,
credit losses and JV investment dilute returns?
This is independent, scenario-based research for discussion. It is not personalized financial advice. Financial figures are consolidated unless stated.
Prices and valuation are dated and can change.
Jio Financial Services | Research snapshot | 20 Oct 2026
JFSL is a financial holding and operating company with lending, payments, asset management, broking, leasing and insurance
activities. Its model pairs proprietary digital distribution with regulated businesses and partner-led JVs. The platform is still in
build-out, so headline app reach and AUM should not be read as mature recurring earnings.

Distribution and capital: the Jio brand and digital channels can lower customer acquisition costs and connect lending, investing,
payments and protection products. A substantial balance sheet can fund the build-out, while BlackRock and Allianz add
Operating inflection: Jio Credit’s AUM and disbursements are growing quickly, and FY26 net income from business operations
reached Rs 1,390 crore, up fourfold year on year. If fee income and lending spreads outpace funding and credit costs, group
earnings could compound from a low base.
Partnership optionality: the announced Bank of America agreement to acquire up to 49.9% of Jio Credit could bring capital and
strategic support if completed. The closing remains subject to approvals and transaction terms; it is not yet realized value.
Why it matters / what to monitor
AUM and disbursements are accelerating. Track delinquencies, write-offs, credit cost by product and vintage,
A larger loan book requires stable liabilities. Rising borrowing costs or weak lending spreads can absorb
Five JVs reported a combined share of loss of Rs 52.7 crore in Q2 and Rs 106.7 crore in H1. Segment
reporting does not yet make every venture’s contribution easy to value.
Low pricing and broad product launches may attract users but can make unit economics difficult. App users,
payment value and AUM are not equivalent to revenue or profit.
Lending, payments, insurance and asset management carry distinct RBI, SEBI and IRDAI requirements. New
ventures and any dilution should be assessed against returns on capital.
Related-party operating arrangements, subsidiaries and JVs raise the importance of transparent reporting,
Q3 FY27 results: AUM growth alongside credit costs and collections; Jio Credit funding costs and profitability; JioBlackRock
fee income and contribution; progress on Bank of America approvals and funding; payments monetization; and whether group
JV losses narrow as new ventures gain scale.
A constructive update would show lending growth with stable asset quality, rising recurring non-interest income, and lower or
more clearly explained JV losses. AUM growth without returns, customer growth without monetization, or continued
deterioration in consolidated earnings would weaken the thesis.

Because a consistent public consensus estimate set was not verified, we use a simple forward earnings sensitivity. These are
our assumptions, not company guidance or a price target from an exchange-registered analyst. FY29 profit is translated to
per-share earnings using about 659 crore shares; the selected P/E multiple reflects the uncertainty and growth embedded in
Scenario values are highly sensitive to both earnings conversion and the multiple. The base case assumes PAT grows to roughly 2.5 times FY26 over
three years; even then, the illustrative upside from the reference price is about 11%. The bear case captures slower lending conversion, higher funding
or credit costs and persistent JV losses. The bull case assumes strong scale and meaningful operating leverage.
Recommendation: HOLD | 12-month base value: Rs 237 | Conviction: Medium-low
At the reference price, the upside in our base case is not large enough to offset the broad execution range. The stock may suit
investors who accept a multi-year platform build and volatile near-term earnings; investors seeking proven returns on equity or
stable earnings may prefer to wait for clearer credit and JV profitability evidence.
